title: Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance - Long Sword | Boosted Action Breakdown
downloaded_with: yt-dlp 2026.08.19, format 135+140 (854x480 h264 30fps + aac 44.1k stereo), merged to mp4
note: Third-party copyrighted promotional video, downloaded for local testing only.

realbasicvsr_export.padding: 854 -> 864 (not a multiple of 32), so 864x480 into the model
realbasicvsr_export.speed: ~1.0 s/frame (0.97-1.14), so the 65 s clip is ~32 minutes
realbasicvsr_export.alignment: export frame N == source frame N (frame 45 matches at 30.8 dB, next best 17.0); best spatial shift (0,0) for every mode

grids.grid_rpt_titlecard.png: frame 45, RP-T title card: source / bypass / cnn / metalfx / realbasicvsr

realesrgan_check.why: A user reported that the shipped Real-ESRGAN mode 'looks bad on real video that's not anime'. This clip is the right material to check that on: genuine natively-degraded 480p, not a synthetic downscale.
realesrgan_check.modes_compared: source(nearest 4x) / bypass / Anime4K CNN / MetalFX Spatial / Real-ESRGAN animevideov3 / Real-ESRGAN general-x4v3, at frame 45, output 3416x1920
realesrgan_check.finding: animevideov3 replaces fine stochastic structure with smooth rounded blobs and expands bright highlights. Most visible on the blue particle effect and the blown specular highlight (grid_real_particles_animevideov3.png): individual sparks become balloons and the highlight loses its internal structure. general-x4v3 shows the same mechanism, slightly less pronounced. The CNN and MetalFX keep the texture.
realesrgan_check.temporal_is_not_the_cause: 40 consecutive frames with real motion: flicker 1.001x the source's own frame-to-frame change (bilinear 0.969x, general-x4v3 1.036x). animevideov3 adds no measurable temporal instability; the artifact is spatial.
realesrgan_check.tone_is_not_the_cause: global luma mean 76.16 against the source's 75.60, saturation 39.10% against 41.15% — far too small to explain the visible difference, which is local structure, not tone.
realesrgan_check.alters_the_picture: mean |output - source| over the 40 frames: bilinear 3.196, animevideov3 5.124, general-x4v3 5.482. It is not sharpening so much as replacing.
realesrgan_check.verification: the Metal port matches PyTorch to 59.99 dB on this model (scripts/realesrgan/verify_metal.py), and the live path matches the offline one to 53.18 dB on this frame — so this is the model's behaviour, not a port artifact.

esrgan_pair_check.why: general-x4v3 was made a live mode (--mode realesrgan-general) so it can be judged on real footage rather than on this project's scores, which come almost entirely from synthetic lanczos downscales. This is the artifact for that judgment.
esrgan_pair_check.how: scripts/realesrgan/pair_grid.sh -- one frame (45) through the live path in bypass/realesrgan/realesrgan-general at 4x, alongside the source nearest-upscaled 4x, cropped 1:1 at 3x.
esrgan_pair_check.alignment: checked, not assumed: the dumped frame matches source frame 45 at 31.63 dB against 17.41 dB for frame 44, so the dump and the extraction are the same frame.
esrgan_pair_check.grids: grid_real_highlight_esrgan_pair.png (blown specular highlight and blue effect), grid_real_foliage_esrgan_pair.png (foliage/rock texture), grid_real_rating_card_esrgan_pair.png (flat UI text) -- panels left to right: source / bilinear / AnimeVideo-v3 / General-x4v3
esrgan_pair_check.what_the_panels_show: On the flat rating-card text both checkpoints resolve esrb.org more cleanly than bilinear, and they are close to each other -- the case the scores rate them on. On the specular highlight and the blue energy effect both replace structure: the highlight loses its internal detail and the blue region becomes a smooth balloon. On foliage the two differ most: general-x4v3 blows the green leaves into larger white specular areas than animevideov3 does. So on this clip general-x4v3 is not simply 'the same but worse' -- it is worse in a different way, which is what the crop pair is for.
esrgan_pair_check.real_time: animevideov3 0.92x realtime and general-x4v3 0.63x at 854x480 -> 3416x1920 (the graph warms up over the first seconds), so at this size general-x4v3 drops about a third of the frames. Judge the picture, not the smoothness.
esrgan_pair_check.memory: 139 MB resident at 480x270 -> 1080p (animevideov3), 295/301 MB at 854x480 -> 3416x1920 -- inside the 2 GB model budget by an order of magnitude.
esrgan_pair_check.licence_note: This clip is third-party promotional material kept for local testing only (test-media/yt/README.md). The grids are derived from it and carry the same restriction: do not redistribute.
